ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word begins with the voiced sound /d/? (1 mark)
   A. den
   B. few
   C. fan
   D. ten

2. When you say 'leaf' and 'leave' aloud, what is the last sound of 'leave'? (1 mark)
   A. /t/
   B. /v/
   C. /d/
   D. /f/

3. Which word comes last in alphabetical order? (1 mark)
   A. sister
   B. brother
   C. aunt
   D. uncle

4. What is a signature? (1 mark)
   A. Your name written in your own handwriting
   B. Your grade
   C. Your telephone number
   D. Your date of birth

5. Which word means a very big and special meal? (1 mark)
   A. snack
   B. ribbon
   C. feast
   D. chore

6. To make the /l/ sound, the tip of the tongue (1 mark)
   A. touches the top lip
   B. touches the bottom lip
   C. touches the ridge behind the top front teeth
   D. stays far from the roof of the mouth and curls back

7. What is the plural of 'baby'? (1 mark)
   A. babies
   B. baby
   C. babys
   D. babyes

8. We answer comprehension questions best in (1 mark)
   A. drawings only
   B. one letter
   C. numbers only
   D. full sentences

9. Which word has a silent h at the start? (1 mark)
   A. house
   B. hour
   C. hand
   D. hen

10. A roundabout is (1 mark)
   A. a railway
   B. a circular junction where vehicles go around in one direction
   C. a straight road
   D. a type of bridge

11. In the word 'emergency', which syllable is stressed? (1 mark)
   A. The second
   B. The first
   C. The third
   D. The fourth

12. Which phrase has adjectives in the correct order? (1 mark)
   A. a red round small ball
   B. a round red small ball
   C. a small round red ball
   D. a round small red ball

13. Which sentence compares Kevin and Musa correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Kevin is more taller than Musa.
   B. Kevin is tall than Musa.
   C. Kevin is taller than Musa.
   D. Kevin is tallest than Musa.

14. Which is the correct order for the parts of a narrative? (1 mark)
   A. End, beginning, middle
   B. Middle, end, beginning
   C. Beginning, middle, end
   D. End, middle, beginning

15. In the email dialogue, which button did they click first to write a new message? (1 mark)
   A. Compose
   B. Save
   C. Send
   D. Reply

16. Which word has the /ʤ/ sound at the beginning? (1 mark)
   A. treasure
   B. chair
   C. yellow
   D. giraffe

17. What is a plough? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of fertilizer
   B. A place for storing tools
   C. A tool or machine used to turn over soil before planting
   D. A small insect that damages crops

18. What should your voice do at the end of a question when reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Stay flat
   B. Stop suddenly
   C. Rise
   D. Fall to a whisper

19. Which is a good strategy for improving fluency? (1 mark)
   A. Re-reading the same passage several times
   B. Reading only the pictures
   C. Skipping hard words
   D. Reading each word very slowly with long stops

20. How do we speak about people who are ill? (1 mark)
   A. By ignoring them
   B. With jokes
   C. With care and respect
   D. With fear

21. In which word does 'gh' say /f/? (1 mark)
   A. daughter
   B. high
   C. laugh
   D. night

22. Which is NOT a way in which HIV spreads? (1 mark)
   A. From a mother to her baby
   B. Sharing sharp objects that have blood on them
   C. Sitting together in class
   D. Through blood

23. Why should water from rivers be boiled before drinking? (1 mark)
   A. It is too cold
   B. It is too clear
   C. It tastes sweet
   D. It may contain germs

24. Which is a better describing phrase than 'nice room'? (1 mark)
   A. a room
   B. a room room
   C. the room, room
   D. a bright, tidy room

25. Which word has the sound /aʊ/? (1 mark)
   A. crowd
   B. cat
   C. bell
   D. hot

26. Which sentence uses the correct word? (1 mark)
   A. I no the answer.
   B. I noe the answer.
   C. I nose the answer.
   D. I know the answer.

27. What does 'Many hands make light work' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Hands are heavy
   B. Work must be light
   C. Big hands are strong
   D. A job is easier when many people help

28. Which sentence uses the right tense with the time word 'yesterday'? (1 mark)
   A. I have saw him yesterday.
   B. I had seen him yesterday now.
   C. I have seen him yesterday.
   D. I saw him yesterday.

29. Which preposition completes: 'She put the coins ____ the tin.'? (1 mark)
   A. into
   B. beside
   C. opposite
   D. between

30. Which is the correct -ing form of 'sit'? (1 mark)
   A. siting
   B. siteing
   C. sittting
   D. sitting

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. List three places where we use a capital letter. (3 marks)

32. Name the seven coordinating conjunctions. (3 marks)

33. Write one sentence with 'enough ... to' and one with 'a lot of' about your school. (3 marks)

34. From the passage about Mama Neema, what can you tell about her character? Give a reason. (3 marks)

35. Rewrite in the past tense: 'I watch a video and I learn a new word.' (2 marks)

36. Write a question for each answer: (a) 'It is at the stadium.' (b) 'The coach.' (2 marks)

37. Join with a suitable conjunction: 'I was tired. I finished sweeping.' (2 marks)

38. Put these events in order: (a) Omondi scored a goal. (b) Baraka spoke to Omondi. (c) The barber changed the blade. (3 marks)

39. Write one sentence using 'present' as a noun and one using 'present' as a verb. Show the stress with capital letters. (3 marks)

40. State two habits of a good listener. (2 marks)

41. Explain what it means to speak with expression. (2 marks)

42. Describe the five-finger test for choosing a book. (4 marks)

43. Explain how you can feel the difference between /t/ and /d/ using your throat. (2 marks)

44. When is it right to interrupt a speaker, and how should you do it? (3 marks)

45. Why is it important to use polite words? Give two reasons. (4 marks)

46. Explain how intonation can change the meaning of 'Really?' (3 marks)

47. Explain the difference between 'good' and 'well'. Give one sentence for each. (4 marks)

48. Write an introduction of two sentences for the topic 'A day I enjoyed'. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — den
   Den starts with /d/, which makes your throat buzz. Ten starts with /t/ and fan and few with /f/.

2. B — /v/
   Leave ends with the voiced sound /v/.

3. D — uncle
   u comes after a, b and s.

4. A — Your name written in your own handwriting
   A signature shows that you agree with what is written.

5. C — feast
   A feast is a large special meal.

6. C — touches the ridge behind the top front teeth
   For /l/ the tongue tip touches the ridge and air flows around the sides.

7. A — babies
   A consonant comes before y, so change y to i and add es.

8. D — full sentences
   Full sentences show that we understand.

9. B — hour
   Hour begins with a vowel sound, so the h is silent.

10. B — a circular junction where vehicles go around in one direction
   Traffic moves round a central island.

11. A — The second
   We say e-MER-gen-cy.

12. C — a small round red ball
   The order is size, shape, colour.

13. C — Kevin is taller than Musa.
   Use the er form with than.

14. C — Beginning, middle, end
   Stories move from beginning to end.

15. A — Compose
   They clicked Compose.

16. D — giraffe
   In 'giraffe' the g says /ʤ/.

17. C — A tool or machine used to turn over soil before planting
   The plough breaks up soil ready for planting.

18. C — Rise
   A question ends with a rising voice.

19. A — Re-reading the same passage several times
   Each re-reading improves speed and expression.

20. C — With care and respect
   People who are ill need care, not fear.

21. C — laugh
   'Gh' says /f/ in laugh, cough, enough and rough.

22. C — Sitting together in class
   Ordinary contact such as sitting together does not spread HIV.

23. D — It may contain germs
   Boiling kills germs.

24. D — a bright, tidy room
   Exact adjectives give a clearer picture.

25. A — crowd
   'Crowd' has the diphthong /aʊ/, as in 'cow'.

26. D — I know the answer.
   'Know' means to have learnt something.

27. D — A job is easier when many people help
   Sharing work makes it easier.

28. D — I saw him yesterday.
   Use the simple past with a finished time such as yesterday.

29. A — into
   She moved the coins to the inside.

30. D — sitting
   Sit doubles the t.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: The first word of a sentence; the word I; names of people; names of places; days and months (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for all seven, 2 for five or six, 1 for three or four.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: We have enough desks to seat every learner. The school has a lot of trees.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pattern and 1 mark for correct punctuation.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: She is kind and patient. When Cherop pulled up a maize plant by mistake she did not scold but gently explained how to tell weeds from maize.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a trait, 2 marks for the reason.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: I watched a video and I learned (learnt) a new word.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for watched, 1 mark for learned/learnt.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) Where is it? (b) Who is the man with the whistle?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable question.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: I was tired, but I finished sweeping.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a suitable conjunction (but or yet) and 1 for the comma.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: (c), (b), (a)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct position.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: My uncle gave me a PRE-sent. I will pre-SENT the prize to the winner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence and 1 mark for correct stress.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker and keep quiet until the speaker has finished a whole idea. Nodding to show you follow is also correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct habit.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means using the voice to show meaning and feeling by changing loudness, stress and pitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using the voice and 1 for showing feeling or meaning.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Open the book at a page and read it. Hold up a finger for every word you do not know. Five fingers means too hard; one to three fingers is a good fit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reading a page, 1 for counting unknown words with fingers, 1 for what five fingers means, 1 for what one to three fingers means.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put your fingers on your throat and say the sounds. You feel a buzz with /d/ because it is voiced, but no buzz with /t/, which is whispered.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the buzz with /d/, 1 mark for no buzz with /t/.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: When you did not hear or understand, or someone needs urgent help. Say politely: 'Excuse me, may I say something?'
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the reasons and 1 for a polite phrase.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Polite words show respect and make people feel welcome. They help people to cooperate and be friendly.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each reason.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: A high rising voice shows surprise, while a low falling voice shows the speaker is not interested. So the tune of the voice shows feelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way and 1 mark for linking to feelings.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: 'Good' is an adjective and describes a noun: She is a good singer. 'Well' is an adverb and describes a verb: She sings well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for each sentence.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: It was a sunny Sunday in Kisumu. My family went to the lake for a picnic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for when or where and 1 mark for who or what.
